tara-cs: FYI, Gridline (dedicated us-west) hit a hard failure this morning during their 08:00 traffic ramp. They reported a big spike in latency and a handful of 5xx responses. They claim the pool never scaled above the tenant min (2) despite sustained ~80 RPS for ~3m. Can someone triage? cc @alex @sam :rotating_light:

alex: Thanks — can you attach their timeline & any logs? Do we see probe failures / pull errors? Also, what were their min/max replica settings?

tara-cs: Min=2, Max=50 per their config. Timeline: 07:59 → gradual ramp; 08:01 → errors start; 08:04 → support gets ticket. Customer provided a short curl repro: `for i in {1..200}; do curl -sS -w '%{http_code}\n' -o /dev/null https://api.redwood.example/endpoint & done`

sam: digging into autoscaler logs for that cluster now. Quick note: I see many "attach_queue_length" spikes coincident with the window. Also several warm-pool pods stuck in Ready=false with probe failures. Posting relevant autoscaler lines below:

```
2026-05-12T07:59:58Z autoscaler[scale-decision] info attach_queue_length=42 target_util=0.65
2026-05-12T08:00:12Z autoscaler[scale-decision] warn suppress_scaleup: attach_queue>backoff_threshold (42>30)
2026-05-12T08:01:05Z runtime[warmpool-manager] warn pod/warmpool-7c9 Unready: init-check-failed
2026-05-12T08:02:30Z autoscaler[scale-decision] info decision=defer warmup_in_progress=true
```

sam: It looks like the autoscaler suppressed aggressive scaleups because the attach queue exceeded a configured threshold. Meanwhile warm-pool pods are failing readiness for ~30-90s due to an init hook (KV cache priming) which delays them from contributing capacity. Result: we never counted the new pods as ready, so we stayed at min replicas.

maria: Any sign of registry/image pull errors (429s) or IAM denies? If pulls are slow, warm pool still stuck.

sam: No image pull 429s in that timeframe. kubelet logs show the init container doing heavy S3/KV fetch and timing out on the first attempt, then succeeding on retry. That means readiness toggles off for longer than expected.

alex: Two quick routes: 1) short-term: recommend manual scale bump for Gridline and increase warmup concurrency for their pool; 2) longer-term: tweak autoscaler heuristics so attach_queue suppression has a fallback path when attach_queue->warm_pod_backlog AND time_since_last_success > X.

tara-cs: Gridline asked for immediate mitigation — I bumped their dedicated pool to 6 manually and they reported error rate dropping. I told them were investigating root cause.

sam: Proposed repro to run in a staging tenant to validate: 1) set min_replicas=2, warm_pool=3 with init-hook that sleeps 20s and fails first probe; 2) generate sustained 60-100 RPS; 3) observe attach_queue + autoscaler suppression + readiness toggles.

maria: Sounds good. Also want to capture metrics: attach_queue_length, warmpool_unready_count, scale_decision_reason. Can someone add a dashboard panel for that timeframe?

sam: I'll export the logs and metrics to the incident bucket and add a short grafana panel for the tenant. Quick mitigation idea: reduce "attach_queue_backoff_threshold" from 30→20 for affected hosts (safer fallback) or add a forced probe after warm pod init completes. Need eng-runtime to weigh in on safe defaults.

oncall-bot: @eng-oncall assign sam — incident 2026-05-12-uw-autoscale-01 created :eyes:

alex: I'll loop in eng-runtime and eng-platform: @maria @sam please include the warmpool init-hook details and metrics export. We should also check if the warmup init hooks are doing heavier-than-expected KV priming after our recent kernel patch.

tara-cs: Customer is happy with manual bump but wants a permanent fix. I'll keep them updated. Thanks team.
